run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. This
started in the last few hours. Please investigate the root cause using the
app-259-prod-logs index.

report.summary: No telemetry exists in any source I could query for the cluster named in the question, production-us-east-2. The requested log index app-259-prod-logs is the only index in the Elasticsearch target and every one of its 9 documents inside the full authorized window 2026-11-20T05:39:59Z–2026-11-21T05:39:59Z carries cluster=production-eu-west-2 and region=eu-west-2; a term query for cluster=production-us-east-2 returned no documents (status no_data, so this is recorded as a gap, not a fact). Those same documents, which describe a DIFFERENT cluster (production-eu-west-2), record an eu-west-2 checkout/payment-provider timeout episode between 2026-11-21T02:39:49Z and 05:34:49Z (checkout-service 500s naming payment-service and payment-provider endpoint /v68/payments, including circuit-breaker-open messages at 04:39:49Z and a recovery line at 05:34:49Z); per the rules for cross-cluster data I do not treat that as the cause of the production-us-east-2 incident. Prometheus (metrics) and Jaeger (traces) were consistently SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE in this Run, so error rates, latency and call paths could not be checked anywhere, and the change_history integration is not integrated. The only Kubernetes cluster I can read is a single-node cluster (node opspilot-m1-control-plane, whose objects carry no topology.kubernetes.io/region label, so its region was not verified from cluster data); its checkout Deployment and pod looked ready with no error log lines in the sampled subset, but that is not evidence about production-us-east-2. No root cause can be named for the reported incident on the available evidence.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch target holds exactly one index, app-259-prod-logs, with 9 documents and 9.6kb store size; no other index is present in the target at the moment of the query.

app-259-prod-logs maps the fields cluster, region, service, level, status_code, correlation_id, message and timestamp — there is no production/us-east-2 specific field beyond these, and cluster and region are keyword fields.

Over the whole authorized window 2026-11-20T05:39:59Z–2026-11-21T05:39:59Z, all 9 documents in app-259-prod-logs aggregate to cluster=production-eu-west-2 (9/9) and region=eu-west-2 (4/4 in the narrower hour, all clusters in the wide window production-eu-west-2), with services checkout-service (6) and payment-service (3) and levels ERROR (6), WARN (2), INFO (1); the documents' own timestamps run 2026-11-21T02:39:49Z to 2026-11-21T05:34:49Z.

The 9 documents retrieved from app-259-prod-logs, all labelled cluster=production-eu-west-2 / region=eu-west-2, record this sequence from a different cluster: checkout-service WARN 'Latency on POST /api/checkout p95=1800ms (target 800ms)' at 02:39:49Z; checkout-service ERROR status_code 500 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s' and payment-service ERROR status_code 504 'Upstream timeout calling provider /v68/payments after 30000ms' at 03:39:49Z; two checkout-service ERROR 500s 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 38% > 25% threshold)' / 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service' at 04:39:49Z; payment-service ERROR 504 upstream timeout at 04:54:49Z; checkout-service ERROR 500 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway' at 05:09:49Z; payment-service WARN 'Payment provider degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=842' at 05:24:49Z; checkout-service INFO 'Recovery: circuit-breaker half-open, success rate 92% over last 60s' at 05:34:49Z.

For the production-eu-west-2 cluster only (NOT the cluster named in the question), the log text points at the external payment provider endpoint /v68/payments being slow/unavailable: the checkout 500s are attributed in the messages to 'payment provider response timeout', 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway' and an open circuit breaker on payment-service, with a 504 upstream timeout on payment-service. The provider itself is outside every queried data source, so its own fault is unverified.

In the Kubernetes cluster I can read (single node opspilot-m1-control-plane; no topology.kubernetes.io/region or zone label on the node), all 21 Deployments in namespace otel-demo report 1/1 ready and 1/1 available, including checkout with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, and the namespace's 22 pods are all Running with the checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n ready and restart count 1.

Application logs of pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n in the readable cluster show, in 294 lines read for the window, only two lines matching an error-oriented filter and both are informational ('payment went through (transaction_id: 61b9c658-...)' at 04:54:41.547Z and 'order confirmation email sent to "bill@example.com"' at 05:34:34.500Z); no error/exception/panic/500/timeout log line was returned for that pod. This concerns the readable cluster only, not production-us-east-2, and the 289 filtered-out lines are unknown.

Cluster-wide events (13 events, only those timestamped 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z–05:38:57Z) concern only namespace app-100a: rollout Normal events for loki-66445c6d6f-27wwv and payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-6w458, and one Warning Endpoints 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints "loki" already exists'. No event in the readable cluster names checkout or a failed pod, and these are not evidence about production-us-east-2.

Rejected as the cause of the reported production-us-east-2 incident: the checkout 500/payment-provider-timeout episode visible in app-259-prod-logs. It is rejected as this incident's cause because every one of those documents is labelled cluster=production-eu-west-2 / region=eu-west-2 and lies in a different cluster's telemetry window (02:39:49Z–05:34:49Z, with its own explicit recovery line at 05:34:49Z); nothing ties it to production-us-east-2.

gaps: No telemetry for production-us-east-2: an Elasticsearch term query for cluster=production-us-east-2 on app-259-prod-logs returned zero documents (status no_data), and the only cluster value present in the index is production-eu-west-2, so the reported us-east-2 checkout failures are unverified and unnamed.

Prometheus was unreachable throughout the Run: get_all_labels, get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (source_contact 'possible'), so error-rate, latency, rpc and kube-state-metrics series for any cluster could not be checked; a missing ERROR series is unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, status code, parent-child edge or call chain could be observed for checkout, payment or any other service.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this environment, so deployments, rollbacks, config or feature-flag changes around 2026-11-20/21 could not be checked for either cluster.

The identity/region of the Kubernetes cluster I can read was not verifiable from its own data: its single node opspilot-m1-control-plane carries no topology.kubernetes.io/region or zone label, and it contains only namespaces app-100a, default, kube-* , local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo — not the workload namespace of either production cluster.

Whether the eu-west-2 payment provider (endpoint /v68/payments) or the payment-service dependency behind it is still degraded cannot be checked: the index has no document newer than 2026-11-21T05:34:49Z and no metric or trace source was available.
No document, metric, trace or object was found that reports the production-us-east-2 customers' 500 errors, so which service, operation or dependency is failing there remains unknown.
next_steps: Obtain telemetry for production-us-east-2 (log index or shipping pipeline, Prometheus and Jaeger endpoints for that cluster) and re-run this investigation there; the current index only covers production-eu-west-2.
Restore or authorize Prometheus and Jaeger access for this Run so checkout/payment error rates, span status codes and RPC durations can be measured rather than inferred from log text.

Confirm with the on-call team whether the production-us-east-2 report might actually refer to the production-eu-west-2 checkout/payment-provider episode recorded between 02:39:49Z and 05:34:49Z, since that is the only checkout failure telemetry present.

If eu-west-2 is in scope, check the external payment provider /v68/payments status page and its retry-queue depth (842 at 05:24:49Z) and confirm whether the 05:34:49Z circuit-breaker recovery held after the last available log document.
Enable the change_history integration so the deployment/flag/config changes that preceded either episode can be inspected (none could be read in this Run).
